chapter_title: Concerning the Fifteen Paths; and whether the Cate
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


---


**
¶2**


Fifteen distinct
 states
 of spiritual progression exist
 within the intermediate region
 of the human mind. Four of these
 states
 are pure and belong to divine
 wisdom
;
 they lead the soul directly
 up
ward toward heavenly life. Eight further
 states are mixed, containing
 both truth
 and falsity, good
 and evil inter
mingled. Whatever
 genuine
 wisdom dw
ells within
 these mixed states asc
ends and is set
 free through
 them; it is purified and received
 into the
 doctrinal forms that carry it toward
 the Divine. But
 the falsity and evil within
 those
 same
 states is
 separated out and cast down
ward into recurring bond
age to
 the
 natural
 self
 and
 its del
usions.
 And
 the remaining
 three states belong
 entirely to evil and fals
ity;
 they are disch
arged into
 the h
ells.

---


**¶3**

The
 three states consigned wholly
 to hell originate from the proprium
 —
 the selfhood of the unre
generate natural man. The
 first is the lust of the will
 against divine order:
 the appetite
 for what
 transg
resses the law of heaven
,
 which
 res
ides
 in every
 person
 and in every
 degree
 of merely
 natural life
. The second is the
 destruction of spiritual life through hatred —
 the impul
se by
 which every
 natural
 faculty
 is consumed
 and ann
ihilated from
 within. The third is prof
anation:
 the deliberate violation of divine good
 con
joined with divine truth in
 its
 redem
ptive suffering
, and
 the w
ounding of every
 living
 form
 that
 contains
 it
 —
 together
 with all
 persu
asion of falsity and
 all
 blasphemy that
 ass
aults
 what
 is divine.

---

**
¶4**

Every
 soul
 follows
 the
 trajectory
 of its own spiritual
 works
,
 whether toward
 heav
enly life or toward spiritual
 death.

---

**¶
15**

Now
 this process
 is understood
 by
 the
 following
 lik
eness.
 The
 ruling
 love of
 a
 person
 dw
ells as
 a sovereign
 within
 the central
 doctrine
 of the mind
,
 while
 all
 its
 derivative affections and thoughts are distributed
 throughout the particular
 states of understanding
,
 memory
, and perception
 that
 compose
 the whole
 interior
 life
.
 As long as this
 ruling
 love remains
 established
 in
 its
 place, all
 subordin
ate aff
ections and thoughts are found
 dwelling
 in
 the surrounding
 states
 that
 depend
 upon it. But
 when
 the moment
 comes
 for
 departure
 from
 the natural
 condition
 —
 when the ruling love gives
 the sign of
 transition
 —
 an
 indication passes
 from
 the in
most will into
 every
 derivative aff
ection and thought, so that each
 may
 set out upon
 its
 own spiritual
 way
 and depart from
 whatever
 state
 it pres
ently occupies,
 moving
 toward the place that
 properly
 belongs to it.


---

**¶16**


Among
 all
 that
 belongs
 to this
 ruling
 love, some aff
ections and thoughts have
 already
 been purified and travel
 ahead
 of it, arriving
 in
 the spiritual
 world
 before
 the person
's
 own
 passage
. Others remain
 bound to it and travel with it,
 depar
ting at the very
 moment of its
 departure
. And still
 others follow
 after
 it, traveling behind
,
 remaining
 for long
 seasons
 and extended
 states
 of grad
ual liberation
 until at
 last they arrive.

---

**
¶17**

The whole
 of what
 belongs to the ruling love does
 not depart at a single moment.
 Rather
, some
 things
 go first,
 others
 follow after, and
 others de
part simultaneously
 with
 it
.

---

**¶18
**

For
 there
 are among
 a
 person's spiritual
 fac
ulties and
 works of
 charity some that are purified while the
 soul
 still
 inhab
its the natural
 body.
 These
 are refined
 through
 the interior
 rational
 states of the heavens and asc
end before the person
. There
 are also among a person's spiritual
 faculties some
 that are lib
erated together
 with the ruling love at
 the very
 moment when
 it departs from
 the natural body
. And
 there are others still
 that
 are freed only
 afterward
 —
 released
 gradually
 from bond
age to earth
ly attach
ments and from
 the hold
 of merely
 natural aff
ections —
 until
 at last they go
 forth
 and reach the person
 in heaven
,
 which
 is the land of the living.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: 'Fifteen paths are drawn out in the zone. Four paths are pure and belong [to the] light, leading up to life. Eight other paths are [mixed], leading above from that place. The light shall go [u]p and become free through them; be purified and go in [to the] ships. However, the waste is separated and thrown [dow]n to transmigr[a]tion and the other three paths of [waste are] discharged to the gehennas'.

[That the three] paths that belong to waste, the ones that are drawn to the gehennas, [a]re drawn from the fleshes. O[n]e of them is the appetite for [lawl]essness, that of people and of all flesh. The second is the [wrath against] all bodies, which is slaughter, [with] which all flesh is consumed. The third is the damaging action, which [injures] the Cross of Light and every body; together with the rest of the error and the blasphemy that wounds the gods.
Th[ese th]ree paths [of waste] lead to the gehennas. And every person shall follow after hi[s] de[e]ds, whether to life or indeed to death.
